metadata.title: Happy LOHRI from PUNJAB ! Rustic PB Food - Makke ki Roti + Saag l Alsi Panjiri & Masala Gud Recipe
metadata.description:
0:00-0:25 - Introduction     
0:25-1:45 - Bhangra Dance
1:46-2:33 - Walk around AGC organic farm
2:34-4:23 - Traditional meal preparation
4:24-5:17 - Tractor ride
5:18-10:34 - Enjoying a typical winter special Punjabi meal
10:35-14:36  Masala gur preparation
14:37-17:47 Alsi ki pinni preparation 
17:48-21:34 Short Introduction about the recipe book
21:35-24:35 Completion of Alsi ki pinni preparation
24:36-25:51 Felicitation and Lohri Celebration

On the auspicious occasion of Lohri, we bring you a slice of Punjab's rich and vibrant culture and food, that we got to experience with the amazing students and faculty members of Amritsar Group Of Colleges' Agricultural Department and the inspiring members of Amritsar based women organization named Phulkari-Women of Amritsar. 

Lohri is celebrated to mark the beginning of the harvest season for winter crops. Every year, during the month of Paush, a day before Makar Sankranti, it is celebrated by the People of Punjab and a few other states with much fanfare. 

During our Amritsar visit we had spent a day with the above team at AGC Agro Farm in Sukhewal village. They had arranged for an immersive cultural experience at this 100 percent certified organic farm of Amritsar Group of Colleges. 

On reaching there along with our city host Deepak Kumar, Founder Amritsar Walking Tours, we received a warm welcome by Ms. Ragini Sharma, Director Of AGC College, Professor Parminder Singh, some of Agriculture Department's students and the lovely members of Phulkari-Women Of Amritsar organization. They all gave us a brief tour of the organic farm that was livened up with winter veggies. The students were dressed up in traditional colourful attire and they all looked so beautiful. This was followed by a mesmerizing Bhangra performance where we too did some steps. 

Then we went on to pluck some veggies and learn more about the current produce in the farm along with Professor Parminder. The sight of the golden mustard flowers adorning the light green mustard leaves made our heart sing with joy. Anubhav couldn't resist himself from giving the iconic Sharukh Khan pose from a popular Bollywood movie which happens in such a setting. 

After this we joined the ladies for the meal preparation in a completely traditional set up. Anubhav helped in the making of green chutney on a traditional stone grind. This was followed by a fun tractor ride that was driven by Anubhav. Tractors are an indispensable part of Punjab's agrarian society. 

Soon the meal was ready and we joined Priyanka Goel and Deepak. The soulful platter consisted of winter special makki di roti, sarson ka saag, aalu meethi, aalu gobhi shalgam achar, rice and jaggery. It is the fundamental winter time meal of the Punjabi community and they are so fond of it.

After this hearty meal we joined Ina Singh ji from Phulkari-Women of Amritsar to learn the recipe of masala gur. This luscious spiced jaggery bite is a winter sweet that can be found in evry Punjabi household. Jaggery are great source of energy and micronutrients and the addition of nuts, carrom seeds, rock salt and dried ginger powder enhances its health benefits.

This was followed by the making of Alsi ki pinni, another healthy and much loved winter time sweet dish from the state. This recipe is of Priyanka Ji's mom, who has always been an advocate of traditional food. Taking her wisdom today Priyanka is running a successful heathy traditional food venture named Aahar Swadam. Moreover, this flaxseeds ladoo recipe also features in Phulkari's Home Food Trail recipe book that brings together best of interesting home recipes from different parts of India.

The slow cooked pinni loaded with ghee and dry fruits was absolutely amazing especially on a chilly day. These cooking sessions are a treasure trove of culinary wisdom and that's why we love such interactions.

This wonderful day culminated with a advanced lohri celebration and it was a truly fun filled experience. We extend our sincere thanks to Amritsar Group Of Colleges and Phulkari-Women Of Punjab for this wonderful and immersive experience.
